Hi Julia / Mike — thanks for a productive session just now. Notes and action items below. Please consider this thread the landing place for follow-ups; Ill upload the attachments to the shared drive link and add them to the HubSpot deal.

Summary (high level):
- We covered Redwood deployment modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and how control boundaries shift with Dedicated/Private.
- Provided SOC 2 highlights: scope (prod inference platform), Type II period (2025-07 to 2026-01), coverage (availability, confidentiality, change management, incident response), and link to SOC 2 summary. Full report is available under NDA / MSA request.
- Walked through the CAIQ: most items are covered by our control suite; we flagged ~12 items that require mapping or additional evidence (see action items).
- Discussed KMS integration for Private: we support customer-managed KMS via KMS/HSM; for Hosted we use cloud provider KMS with tenant separation and envelope encryption.

Detailed Q&A highlights:
Q: How is KV cache data handled for Dedicated vs Hosted?
A: KV cache includes transient tokens that are not stored persistently for hosted sessions. For Dedicated and Private deployments, customers can opt-in to disk persistence; default is in-memory with eviction policies. See SIG Response row 17 for evidence.

Q: Retention & logging — whats the default retention for audit logs?
A: Default retention is 90 days; we offer extended retention (1/3/7 years) as an add-on for Dedicated/Private customers. Logs are write-once, tamper-evident via signed log rotation and stored in encrypted buckets.
